clue.text: Sack little Dolly from the Baltimore branch ?

parts.note: to sack someone is to fire them from a job
a dolly-bird is slang for a pretty young woman, so a little Dolly is a bird

explanation.surface: Someone sacks a young woman from the Baltimore office of a firm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Baltimore branch' sounds like a company office, but it is the bough of a tree where the Baltimore oriole, also called a firebird, perches.
explanation.definitionFit: The Baltimore oriole, a bright orange songbird of North America, is popularly known by this name.

clue.text: Look ahead to reward for services, putting in mineral aggregates

indicators.note: one piece is put into the other, placed within it

parts.note: a fee is payment for professional services
ores are rocks from which minerals are extracted

explanation.surface: Someone looks ahead to payment for services involving mineral deposits.
explanation.definitionFit: To foresee is to anticipate or predict what is coming.

clue.text: Green isn't out of order bearing a grudge

indicators.note: letters of Green isn't put out of their order are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man called Green is not out of line in bearing a grudge.
explanation.definitionFit: To bear a grudge is to feel bitter about a wrong.

clue.text: Tom for instance in one family of painters

parts.note: Great Tom is the famous bell of Christ Church, Oxford
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Tom, for example, belongs to a family of artists.
explanation.walkthrough: Great Tom is a well-known bell at Christ Church, Oxford, so 'Tom for instance' is a bell, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: Jacopo, Gentile and Giovanni were the Venetian Renaissance painting family of this name.

clue.text: Music for occasion of students' frolic

parts.note: a rag is a British student carnival held to raise charity money
an occasion is a time

explanation.surface: Music suitable for a student party.
explanation.walkthrough: A rag is the British student charity week of stunts and parades.
explanation.definitionFit: This syncopated piano music, popularised by Scott Joplin, was an early American popular style.

clue.text: Spotted once-cheap fruit

parts.note: d stood for the old British penny, a price that was once cheap
an apple is a fruit

explanation.surface: Someone spots fruit that used to be cheap.
explanation.walkthrough: D is the abbreviation for the penny in Britain's pre-1971 money, so a once-cheap fruit is a penny apple.
explanation.definitionFit: A dappled horse or surface is marked with spots or patches of colour.

clue.text: Vanish quietly into paradise, maybe

indicators.note: one piece goes into the other, inside it
maybe suggests paradise in some possible other arrangement of its letters

parts.note: p, for piano, means quietly in music

explanation.surface: Someone quietly vanishes into paradise, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' rearranges PARADISE to DISAPEAR, and 'into' puts P inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To disappear is to vanish from sight.

clue.text: The head a short way from the trunk?

definitions.text: The head a short way from the trunk?

parts.words: The head a short way from the trunk?
parts.note: a tree whose crown has been cut back close to its trunk, not a person's head on the torso

explanation.definitionFit: A tree cut back to the trunk so its head of new shoots sprouts just above it is called this.

clue.text: Still to be seen in late outfit of the latest arrival

indicators.note: one word is to be seen inside the other, contained in it

parts.note: taken as written
yet means still, as in not yet done

explanation.surface: Something still visible in a late outfit of the newest arrival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'latest arrival' is a newborn baby, not a late guest.
explanation.definitionFit: A layette is a set of clothing and bedding for a newborn baby.

clue.text: They're wicked to charge the traffic signals

parts.note: to charge at something is to rush at it
traffic signals are traffic lights

explanation.surface: Wicked people charge through the traffic signals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wicked' is not evil here: it means having wicks, which these old candles made of rush pith dipped in fat did.
explanation.definitionFit: Candles of rush pith dipped in tallow each have a wick, so they are wicked things.

clue.text: Songs of the egg-bird?

definitions.meaning: a lay is a short narrative poem or song
what a laying hen does is produce eggs

explanation.surface: A bird's songs are mentioned.
explanation.definitionFit: Lays are old ballads, and a hen lays eggs, so the word fits both the songs and the egg-producing bird's action.

clue.text: Do not touch this machinery, Mimosa

definitions.meaning: machinery that is delicate is ..., plant meaning industrial machinery
the mimosa is a shrub whose leaves fold when touched

explanation.surface: A warning sign beside some equipment, followed by the name of a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: Mimosa pudica folds its leaves when touched, earning its common name; machinery (plant) that must not be touched is delicate.

clue.text: This building is partly protected if ice and snow prevail

indicators.note: only part of the words protected if ice is used, a run of letters inside them

explanation.surface: A building is partly sheltered when ice and snow are prevalent.
explanation.definitionFit: An edifice is a large, imposing building.

clue.text: Pass on the wrong side as the early settlers did

parts.note: a col is a mountain pass
taken as written

indicators.note: the word side set wrong is jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: Overtaking on the wrong side, as pioneers once did.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' scrambles SIDE to ISED; 'Pass' is a mountain col, not overtaking.
explanation.definitionFit: Early settlers established colonies in new lands.

clue.text: Plot for retirement of a good tennis player

parts.note: a seed is a highly ranked tennis player in a tournament draw
one retires to bed at night

explanation.surface: A scheme for the retirement of a fine tennis player.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plot' looks like a scheme, but it is a plot of ground where seeds are sown.
explanation.definitionFit: A plot of ground prepared for sowing seeds is called this.

clue.text: At least Dracula wasn't this sort of slanderer!

definitions.text: At least Dracula wasn't this sort of slanderer!

parts.words: At least Dracula wasn't this sort of slanderer!
parts.note: Dracula bit his victims on the neck from the front, never from behind

explanation.definitionFit: Someone who speaks spitefully of a person behind their back is a slanderer of this sort.

clue.text: " Then — sings the staring owl " (L.L. Lost)

definitions.text: " Then — sings the staring owl " (L.L. Lost)

parts.words: " Then — sings the staring owl " (L.L. Lost)
parts.note: a fill-in quotation from the winter song that closes Love's Labour's Lost, where the owl sings every night

explanation.walkthrough: The song 'When icicles hang by the wall' ends Shakespeare's Love's Labour's Lost; its refrain has the owl singing night after night.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's owl sings every night, which is the missing adverb in the quoted line.

clue.text: Repeat it, quarter price

parts.note: E, for east, is one of the four compass quarters
a rate is a price charged

explanation.surface: Say it again: a quarter of the price.
explanation.definitionFit: To iterate is to say or do something again.

clue.text: Odious way to put the lid on fuel difficulties

indicators.note: in a down clue, the hat is put on top of the other piece

parts.note: lid is slang for a hat

indicators.note: the word fuel in difficulties is thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A nasty way of capping problems with fuel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'difficulties' scrambles FUEL to EFUL, and 'on' puts HAT on top of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something odious is detestable and arouses loathing.

clue.text: Ran about in return set in medium conditions

indicators.note: the first pieces go inside the turned word, as in places them within it
return signals that the word set is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: taken as written before being turned
taken as written
c, short for circa, means about

explanation.surface: Someone ran around, returning to the middle of a group under certain conditions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' turns SET into TES, and 'in' puts RAN plus C inside it. 'medium' is a spiritualist, not middling.
explanation.definitionFit: A spiritualist medium goes into states of trance during seances, so these are the conditions a medium works in.

clue.text: This happy man's motto " Blaze away "?

definitions.text: This happy man's motto " Blaze away "?

parts.words: This happy man's motto " Blaze away "?
parts.note: someone over-eager to shoot, happy to fire at will, lives by that saying

explanation.definitionFit: A trigger-happy person is too quick to fire a gun, as the joined word with happy suggests.

clue.text: They wing their way down from trees

definitions.text: They wing their way down from trees

parts.words: They wing their way down from trees
parts.note: winged seeds that spin down from a particular tree, not birds

explanation.definitionFit: Ash trees shed winged seeds in clusters, called keys for their resemblance to old keys.

clue.text: Sailors', we hear, but rather electricians' inventor

indicators.note: what we hear signals a word that sounds like another one

parts.note: seamen are sailors, so seamen's means belonging to sailors

explanation.surface: Sailors' property, supposedly, but really that of an electrical inventor.
explanation.walkthrough: Werner von Siemens was the German electrical engineer whose name became the SI unit of conductance.
explanation.definitionFit: Werner von Siemens pioneered electrical engineering and founded the firm bearing his name.

clue.text: Break seal with gun exhibit so it can be put out

indicators.note: breaking these words apart lets their letters be rearranged

explanation.surface: Breaking a seal with a gun on display so a fire can be put out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Break' rearranges SEAL, GUN and EXHIBIT; 'with' only joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: A fire that can be put out is able to be quenched.

clue.text: Compare — about a pound for this binding

indicators.note: the abbreviation goes around the other letters, about meaning surrounding them

parts.note: cf is the abbreviation for compare, from Latin confer
l is the abbreviation for a pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A note to compare something costing about a pound for a book's binding.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay builds CALF, a leather used for book bindings; the grid as held prints HALF, one letter away.
explanation.definitionFit: Calfskin leather is a traditional material for covering books.

clue.text: One crawling about with all-male party hangover?

parts.note: a stag party is a party for men only before a wedding
to beetle is to overhang, as beetling brows or cliffs do

explanation.surface: Someone crawling around after an all-male party with a hangover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hangover' is not the morning after: it means something that hangs over, as beetling cliffs do.
explanation.definitionFit: This large insect with antler-like jaws crawls about on the ground.

clue.text: I delve curiously into what is hidden

indicators.note: the letters of I delve are arranged in a curious, odd new order

explanation.surface: I dig inquisitively into what is concealed.
explanation.definitionFit: Something covered by a veil is concealed.

clue.text: Poor type rubber solutions?

parts.note: a rubber here is an eraser, and its solution to badly typed letters is rubbing them out

explanation.definitionFit: Rubbing out mistakes with an eraser produces these, which fix poorly typed text.
